newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Former Merrill employee freed on bail in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Former Merrill employee freed on bail in Hong Kong.

text.p: Kevin Wallace, a former private banking star at Merrill Lynch, posted bail of more than HK$1 million ($129,000) after he was detained earlier this week, police said on Wednesday.
The sum included bail of HK$100,000 in cash and HK$1 million in a personal guarantee. Police said no charges had been filed and Wallace must report to police again on July 16.

He was arrested on Monday night, along with an unidentified Chinese man, and released on Tuesday. The Chinese man was freed on cash bail of HK$100,000. Police had said earlier the second man's bail was HK$500,000.
Police declined to say why Wallace was arrested.
U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch International started civil proceedings against Wallace last month in Singapore and Hong Kong, and filed a criminal complaint in Singapore.
Merrill Lynch accused Wallace of engaging in "unauthorised trading, misrepresenting or falsifying private clients' statements and forging client signatures".
Merrill Lynch spokesman Robert Grieves said the company had not filed a criminal complaint against Wallace in Hong Kong but was cooperating with police in their investigation.
In his job at Merrill, Wallace acted as a financial consultant to high-net worth clients across Asia, taking investment orders and providing investment advice.
The 46-year-old American was employed by Merrill Lynch from late 1991 until he was dismissed on May 15 this year.
Merrill Lynch has not commented on the amount in question in the case, but industry sources and media reports have put it at around US$30 million.
Merrill Lynch has said that the costs it might incur from the alleged fraud would not be "significant to Merrill Lynch's business or financial position."
The company made US$1.6 billion in profits last year.
The investment bank has settled with about half of Wallace's clients, Grieves said. (US$1 = HK$7.74)
